edges.description: The model supplies and reads out healthy human RGCs - the cell population whose death is this node - establishing their identity (BRN3A/SNCG) and functional maturation by electrophysiology and calcium imaging. It measures the substrate of the node; it does not encode a glaucoma lesion and does not reproduce RGC death.
edges.limitations: Wild-type cells with no glaucoma lesion (OPTN, MYOC, elevated intraocular pressure), and developmentally immature relative to the adult neurons that degenerate in glaucoma; the product's identity also depends on the sourcing route, directly differentiated and fetal RGCs predominantly expressing BRN3A where most organoid-derived RGCs express BRN3B.
edges.source: iPSC-derived retinal ganglion cells (canonical differentiation protocols)

nodes.description: Progressive apoptosis of retinal ganglion cells leads to irreversible vision loss. Mechanical stress, ischemia, and excitotoxicity contribute to cell death.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal ganglion cell apoptotic pathway in glaucoma: Initiating and downstream mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: Apoptosis of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) in glaucoma causes progressive visual field loss, making it the primary cause of irreversible blindness worldwide.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in autophagy caused by glaucoma-associated mutations in optineurin.
evidence.snippet: A glaucoma-associated mutant of optineurin, E50K, impairs autophagy as well as vesicle trafficking, leading to death of retinal cells by apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Anti-inflammatory Effects of Siponimod in a Mouse Model of Excitotoxicity-Induced Retinal Injury.
evidence.snippet: Glaucoma is a leading cause of permanent blindness worldwide and is characterized by neurodegeneration linked to progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) death, axonal damage, and neuroinflammation.

experimental_models.name: iPSC-derived retinal ganglion cells (canonical differentiation protocols)

nodes.description: Wild-type human iPSC-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), reviewed across published protocols in PMID:37686457 (Table 2: chemically defined conditions, biomaterial scaffolds for neurite outgrowth, dual-SMAD plus Wnt inhibition, organoid dissociation with magnetic-activated cell sorting, and rapid NGN2 overexpression). RGCs are the projection neuron whose death defines glaucoma, but no glaucoma allele is present, so the model measures the RGC substrate rather than reproducing the neurodegeneration. This is the canonical (non-disease) baseline protocol underlying the isogenic OPTN(E50K) hPSC-derived RGC instance curated on OPTN-related Open Angle Glaucoma; that genotype instance, not this record, carries the RECAPITULATES link for the OPTN autophagy lesion.
